turns.t: Good morning. Could you confirm your name for me, please? I have a Mr. Cyril Abara booked in.
That's... yes, Cyril. Cyril Abara.
Thank you, Cyril. And you are?
I'm Funmi, his daughter. I drove him in. He doesn't like to make a fuss, so I thought I'd better come in and help.
I'm glad you did. Cyril, is it all right with you if Funmi stays and joins in?
Yes, yes. She's... she knows, she hears me every day.
Good. So what brings you here today, in your own words?
It's my voice. It's... gone a bit. Rough, like. Since I was poorly in the winter, I've not, um...
Dad, tell him how it sounds. He sounds like he's been shouting at a football match, doctor, and it's been that way for weeks.
A rough, hoarse voice since the winter illness. Cyril, has it come and gone, or is it the same every day?
Same, mostly. A bit worse at night, maybe. I get tired, and then it's just a... a whisper.
I see. And does it hurt when you speak or swallow? I'm trying to understand if it's the voice itself, or the throat.
Not hurt exactly. It's just... scratchy. I'm not good at describing.
You're doing very well. Now, it's important I ask this because we may need to choose a medicine today. Do you have any allergies?
Well, I... um, there's penicillin. I was told I'm allergic to it.
He came out in a rash all over when he was given it, doctor. After a tooth abscess, I think, years ago. It's on his card but they never look.
Penicillin, with a rash. Thank you, Funmi, that's very helpful. I'll make sure it's noted clearly in your record, Cyril. Any other allergies, to foods or anything?
No, that's the only one I know of.
Good. Let me ask about your background. Any long-term conditions?
I have asthma. Since I was a boy. And my blood pressure, it's a bit high, I'm told.
Asthma and high blood pressure. And in the family, anyone with throat or voice problems, or anything similar?
Not really. My mother had thyroid problems, that's all I can think of.
Thank you. A routine question I ask everyone with a voice change. Do you smoke, or have you ever?
Never. Not once. I never smoked in my life. My father did, and I hated it.
He's very proud of that, doctor.
Rightly so. It makes some of the more worrying causes less likely. Now, let me take a couple of readings. Temperature is 36.6 degrees.
And oxygen saturation is 97 percent, which is perfectly good for you.
Is that all right, then?
It is. Now open wide for me, and say 'aah'. I'll use this light.
The throat is a little red at the back, nothing alarming. Your voice has that husky, breathy quality, as Funmi said. Now let me feel your neck.
Is that where the glands are?
Yes. There are no lumps in the neck on either side, and nothing tender. That's reassuring.
So what is it, doctor? He's been so worried, he won't say, but I can tell.

I'll explain my thinking. After a long illness with a lot of coughing, the voice box can get irritated and inflamed. Stomach acid creeping up at night can keep it irritated and slow the healing. From everything I've seen, that's the most likely explanation.
Acid? I've not had heartburn. Not a lot.
It can happen silently, without heartburn, which is why it's often missed. It's my working idea, not a certainty.
So I'd like to start you on a course of omeprazole, maybe 20 mg once a day, before breakfast. I'll confirm the exact strength when I write the prescription.
Will it have any side effects we should watch for?

Most people notice nothing, though a mild headache or loose stools can happen. For the voice itself, give it rest, avoid whispering, which strains it more than speaking softly, and sip water through the day.
Whispering is worse? I'd never have guessed.
Most people don't. Steam from a bowl of hot water can soothe it, too, as long as you're careful with the kettle.
I'll make sure he's careful. He once burned his hand on the kettle and blamed me.
That's a lie, I blamed the kettle.
I can see the family is in good hands. One last thing, and I want you both to hear it. If you ever have trouble breathing, noisy breathing, or difficulty swallowing, don't wait, call an ambulance.
I understand. Thank you, doctor. I feel... better for having asked.
Good. Funmi, thank you for bringing him. Look after each other.
